cues.zh: 2019年除夕夜，中国卫生官员承认他们遇到了问题。

cues.en: It eventually reached 29 countries and killed nearly 800 people.

cues.en: Now, 18 years later, this coronavirus is in at least 71 countries and has already killed
over 3100 people.

cues.en: potentially infect them.

cues.en: And if the virus then spreads to other humans, it causes an outbreak.

cues.en: Back in the 1970s, China was falling apart.

cues.en: Famine had killed more than 36 million people.

cues.zh: 而控制着所有粮食生产的共产党政权，却无法养活
cues.en: And the communist regime, which controlled all food production, was failing to feed its

cues.en: more than 900 million people.

cues.zh: 1978年，政权濒临崩溃，放弃了这一控制，允许私人务农。
cues.en: In 1978, on the verge of collapse, the regime gave up this control and allowed private farming.

cues.zh: 大型企业日益主导猪肉等大众食品的生产
cues.en: While large companies increasingly dominated the production of popular foods like pork

cues.en: and poultry, some smaller farmers turned to catching and raising wild animals as a way

cues.en: And since it started to feed and sustain people, the Chinese government backed it.

cues.en: But then in 1988, the government made a decision that changed the shape of wildlife trade in
China.

cues.en: They enacted the Wildlife Protection Law which designated the animals as “resources owned

cues.en: by the state” and protected people engaged in the “utilization of wildlife resources”.

cues.en: The law also “encouraged the domestication and breeding of wildlife.”

cues.zh: 由此，一个产业诞生了。
cues.en: With that, an industry was born.

cues.en: Small local farms turned into industrial-sized operations.

cues.en: For example, this bear farm started with just three, and eventually grew to more than 1,000 bears.

cues.zh: 种群规模越大，病畜传播疾病的机会就越大。
cues.en: Bigger populations meant greater chances that a sick animal could spread disease.

cues.zh: 养殖户还饲养着种类繁多的动物。
cues.en: Farmers were also raising a wide variety of animals.

cues.zh: 这意味着农场里的病毒也更多。

cues.en: cover for an illegal wildlife industry.

cues.en: Endangered animals like tigers, rhinoceroses, and pangolins, were trafficked into China.

cues.en: By the early 2000s, these markets were teeming with wild animals when the inevitable happened.

cues.en: It is what health officials have feared all along.

cues.en: In 2003, the SARS outbreak was traced to a wet-market here, in southern China.

cues.en: Scientists found traces of the virus in farmed civet cats.

cues.en: Chinese officials quickly shut down the markets and banned wildlife farming.

cues.en: But a few months after the outbreak, the Chinese government declared 54 species of wildlife

cues.en: And it exerted significant influence over the Chinese government.

cues.en: tigers, and pangolins.
